text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three people were killed and a village burnt in fighting between armed youths of rival Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes despite a peace agreement between their elders to end the two-month-old clashes.
- Panic at Lagos airport as air force officer shoots a luggage handling agent; police say they are investigating the incident and that no one has been arrested yet.
- U.S. embassy in Lagos confirms newspaper reports that one of its Nigerian staff is being questioned by the police over a bomb blast in Lagos on Wednesday.
- Commercial activities in northern Nigerian city of Kano come to a standstill as Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi visits the city and urges unity among African nations.
- Twenty-five prominent lawyers appear as defence attorneys for 12 dissidents charged with treason over spate of bomb explosions in Nigeria.
- Fuel scarcity in Lagos area is traced to closure of a pipeline transporting oil products from Atlas Cove jetty to Ejigbo and Mosimi depots that serve the city.
- U.S. embassy condemns the recent bomb blast in Nigeria and restates its government's "complete rejection of terrorism for any purpose."
- Nigeria and China are to sign an agreement in Abuja on Saturday to cooperate in the petroleum industry.
